sourceOfTruth: This file. docs/handoff/QUEUE.md is RENDERED from it by `node scripts/check-queue.mjs --render` and is verified in sync. Never hand-edit the .md.

twoLedgers.why: A readiness register and a queue are two lists of open things, and two lists of open things become two competing sources of truth within a week unless the boundary is written down and one derives from the other. It is written down here.
twoLedgers.queueOwns: WORK. An item exists here because somebody intends to do it, it is claimable, it has a founderHours price, a window, and a verify command that check-queue --done re-runs at close. Nothing is worked that is not here.
twoLedgers.registerOwns: READINESS. data/readiness-register.json is the ledger of GAPS the 15-domain validation panel found — one record per gap, classified verifiable / decision / opinion. It answers 'is this domain ready', never 'what should I do next'. Its item statuses are RE-DERIVED from exit codes by scripts/check-readiness.mjs, not authored, so it cannot drift into an opinion about itself.
twoLedgers.derivation: ONE-WAY: register → queue. A verifiable, agent-owned register item is PROMOTED into this file by the INTAKE lane of scripts/loop-driver.mjs, which stamps the register record with `queueItem: Q-0NN`. That stamp is the join. A register record carrying a queueItem is no longer a candidate; the queue item is now the only place its work is tracked.
twoLedgers.neverTheOtherWay: The queue never writes back into the register, and a register record is never closed by hand. A promoted gap closes when its QUEUE item closes; check-readiness then re-derives the register's verdict from the same verify command exiting 0.
twoLedgers.decisionsDoNotEnter: A register record classed `decision` has no verify command by construction, so it can never be promoted. It routes to the founder. 18 of 101 loop-eligible records are decisions today — that is the rate limit ADR-034 rule 2 names, and it is why the loop cannot manufacture founder debt by working faster.

doctrine: A queue item is not done because a session says so. It is done when its `verify` command exits 0, re-run at close time by scripts/check-queue.mjs --done, and re-runnable forever after by --verify --all.

A HIGH item that is `ready` (nobody has claimed it) makes scripts/check-queue.mjs exit 1. A scheduled session runs that gate as its FIRST act, so it cannot report a clean run while urgent work sits untouched.
A claim older than staleClaimDays with no closure is released automatically. Bookkeeping does not live in agent memory; a dead session cannot park a HIGH item forever.
Every item cites file:line or a command. Nothing here is an impression.

policy.oneInOneOut: Adding an item whose kind is `mechanism` requires a non-empty `retires` array. Enforced by --self-test.
policy.staleClaimRationale: 21, not 7. Measured burst pattern: 24 of 60 days idle; 266 of 344 storefront commits landed on 8 days (board-execution-feasibility.md). A 7-day expiry released most claims without a state change, so the board churned while nothing moved.
policy.founderHoursAreDeclared: Every item carries founderHours (a number, 0 for pure-agent work) and a window (M1|M2|M3|later). The budget is summed from those fields, never parsed out of the effort prose. Enforced by validate(); checked by --budget.

items.title: check-all is NOT idempotent — two runs give different totals and dirty the working tree
items.why: Measured 2026-08-07 in this container: three consecutive `node scripts/check-all.mjs` runs, no other command between them, returned 311/320, 306/320 and 309/323 — the DENOMINATOR moved. Working-tree dirty count went 208 -> 215 across the runs. The deploy gate writes files while checking, which is why clearing reds locally never converges and why the founder's only feedback loop has a false-alarm rate he has learned to ignore (the board already records PR #536 'merged with three reds the founder accepted'). This is upstream of every other red: until check-all is a pure function of the tree, no agent session can prove it fixed anything.

checkpointPolicy.rule: A checkpoint whose dueOn has passed with result null makes check-queue exit 1, and no amount of closed items clears it. A plan with no falsifier is a wish; a falsifier nobody is forced to read is the same wish with extra steps.
checkpointPolicy.whoRecords: founder — every killIf whose decidedBy is `measurement` is computed from a receipt file, but the decision to proceed, amend or kill is a judgment with a name on it.
checkpointPolicy.amendMeans: The checkpoint's own terms were wrong, not the strategy. An amendment must say what replaced them, or it is a kill being called a proceed.
